one_month_reasoning: No Oracle earnings in the window: Q2 FY27 is on 2026-12-14. Inside the window: (1) the $0.50 dividend goes ex around the Oct 9 record date, which shifts the median down ~$0.50; (2) the Investor Day management promised on the Q1 call for October (date not confirmed; last year's analyst meeting was at AI World, so it likely falls around AI World on Oct 25-28), where it said it would detail margin trajectories and financial strategy. This could bring an FCF-positive date or long-term targets (upside), or a higher capex/financing need (downside); (3) Big-4 Q3 calls (~Oct 28-30) with first 2027 capex guides, which per the standing capex view lean up; (4) FOMC Oct 27-28. Unscheduled: the OpenAI ~$30B raise closing (positive) and further site-delay or Moody's news (negative). Kalshi puts an OpenAI IPO announcement before Nov 1 at ~1%, so it is not a 1-month catalyst. These offset in direction, so I use a symmetric lognormal around ~$142.9 with sigma ~16.6% (56%/3.5, widened ~4% for the Investor Day) and no drift.

fair_value.method: Fair value at Oct-2027: 60% P/E (NTM EPS $11.33 = 8/12 FY28 $10.3 + 4/12 FY29 $13.4, x 15x = $170) and 40% EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA ~$57B x 11.5x = $659B, less ~$140B net debt ex operating leases, over 3.13B shares = $166). Both multiples are inside a 10-peer range, ~30% below the median (P/E median 21.7x CY2027). The scenario-weighted mean is ~$165, ~$3 below fair value, because the bear tail is fatter than the bull tail.

inputs_detail.derivation: Company target $8.10; Yahoo non-GAAP consensus $8.14 (37 analysts).

Non-GAAP consensus $11.00 (Yahoo, 39 analysts, range 9.00-13.30). I haircut ~6% to $10.3 for two reasons only: power-delayed capacity at Wisconsin (Aterio: meaningful load unlikely before mid-2028 vs 2H27 guidance) and Project Jupiter (force majeure), and dilution and interest from the ~$20-40B of further FY27 financing beyond the completed $19.9B ATM. The Fool/Zacks $9.13 figure is a GAAP-like basis and is no longer part of the argument.

No non-GAAP FY29 consensus is published. The Zacks GAAP-like FY29/FY28 ratio is 12.84/9.14 = 1.40 (only 5 estimates), so consensus-implied non-GAAP is ~$15.4. I assume +30% over my $10.3 = $13.4, about 13% below that implied figure, because depreciation ramps on $90-95B/yr capex, AI-infrastructure gross margin keeps falling until the ramp ends (management: margin 'would flatten' only afterwards), and interest cost rises. This replaces my round-1 $12.3, which was ~20% below consensus-implied without saying so.

8/12 x FY28 $10.3 + 4/12 x FY29 $13.4 = $11.33 (FY28 runs Jun-27 to May-28, so 8 of the 12 NTM months fall in FY28; round 1 used 0.6/0.4). Consensus-implied NTM is ~$12.5, so I am ~9% below the street.

Reconciled 10-peer CY2027 median is 21.7x (range 8.5-27.0x; SAP corrected to 21.5x on USD EPS of $9.60). Sub-medians: hyperscalers ~23.7x, enterprise software ~15.6x. 15x is inside the peer range, ~31% below the median and at the enterprise-software sub-median (IBM 16.8x, CRM 14.3x, WDAY 14.2x). The discount rests on features that are checkable and persist through Oct-2027: FY27-28 are guided peak-capex years with no FCF-positive date; TTM FCF is ~-$28.7B; S&P is at BBB- (stable) and Moody's at Baa2 (negative) while the hyperscaler peers are A or better; and ~half of the $664B RPO sits with one loss-making counterparty. ORCL's +35% FY28 EPS growth, the fastest in the set, is why I go no lower.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM revenue ~$133B x 43% = ~$57.3B EBITDA; x 11.5x = $659B EV; less ~$140B net debt (ex operating leases); / 3.13B shares = $166

inputs_detail.derivation: 8/12 x FY28 ~$125B (consensus $131.7B less ~$7B for power-delayed Wisconsin/Jupiter capacity) + 4/12 x FY29 ~$150B.
TTM EBITDA $34.4B on ~$71.8B TTM revenue is ~48%. I take ~5pt off for the guided gross-margin step-down as low-margin AI infrastructure grows. NTM EBITDA is ~$57B.

Peer EV/EBITDA is TTM from stockanalysis (median 17.6x, range 9.4-49.5x). Forward data were not accessible, so I roll each peer's TTM multiple to an approximate forward one by dividing by (1 + next-year EPS growth), using the peer median ~15% where AMZN and GOOGL EPS are distorted by investment gains. That gives a forward peer median of ~16.3x (range 8.4-40.2x). 11.5x is inside the range and ~30% below the median, matching the P/E discount and its reasons. ORCL today is ~15.4x TTM on EV ex operating leases.

inputs_detail.input: Net debt at Oct-2027 (ex operating leases)
inputs_detail.derivation: Notes $125.3B ($7.6B current + $117.7B non-current) less $37.1B cash and securities = $88.2B, plus ~$9B finance leases (finance-lease ROU assets $8.9B per the 10-Q) = ~$97B. Add Q2-Q4 FY27 FCF of about -$32 to -37B (S&P FY27 FOCF ~-$42B less Q1 -$5.4B), Q1 FY28 about -$8B and ~$6B of dividends ($0.50/qtr): ~$145-148B before equity. Less ~$8B of the $20-40B Jan-May 2027 financing taken as equity gives ~$140B. Operating leases (non-current $30.6B) are excluded because EBITDA is after rent. Round 1's $157B was lease-inclusive.
3,024M outstanding after the completed $19.9B ATM (141M shares), plus the Series D mandatory convertible and ~$8-10B of 2027 equity at ~$140-150 (~3.5% in total).

bear.story: Financing and counterparty stress. OpenAI's raise stalls or it re-scopes Stargate commitments, and power delays (Jupiter force majeure, Wisconsin PSC refiling) push $20B+ of revenue past FY28. Moody's cuts to Baa3, and S&P moves to negative outlook on wider FOCF deficits, so the Jan-May 2027 financing skews to dilutive equity. NTM EPS ~$9 at ~10x, or EV/NTM EBITDA ~7.5x on ~$140-150B net debt.

base.story: Capacity keeps landing (Abilene, Shackelford 1H27) despite Wisconsin slipping, and FY28 EPS is ~$10.3 (~6% under consensus). The 2027 financing is absorbed at modest dilution, S&P stays stable, and the Investor Day/FY28 guide gives a credible path to FCF after the peak. The stock trades at 15x NTM EPS (~$11.3), the enterprise-software sub-median, i.e. the fair value.

bull.story: OpenAI closes ~$30B at ~$1.4T and announces an IPO by mid-2027 (Kalshi ~50%), removing the counterparty overhang. RPO conversion accelerates with prepaid/BYO-hardware contracts, management gives an FCF-positive date for FY29, CDS tightens, and the multiple goes to ~20x (still below the 21.7x peer median) on ~$12 NTM EPS.

comps_summary.peer_range: P/E on calendar-2027 non-GAAP consensus (fiscal years calendarised: MSFT avg FY27/FY28; CRM and WDAY FY Jan-28; ADBE FY Nov-27; SAP USD EPS from Zacks): 8.5x (ADBE) to 27.0x (NOW), median 21.7x across 10 peers. This is a single CY2027 basis, not stockanalysis 'Forward PE'. EV/EBITDA: stockanalysis TTM 9.4x-49.5x (median 17.6x), rolled to an approximate forward basis by dividing by (1 + next-year growth): 8.4x-40.2x, median ~16.3x. The forward EV/EBITDA figures are my estimates, not reported forwards. CoreWeave (round 1) is dropped: it is loss-making, its 25.2x was TTM against forward peers, and its forward EBITDA multiple was not verified.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: ORCL is at 14.6x CY2027 consensus EPS ($9.81) and ~15.4x TTM EV/EBITDA (EV ex operating leases). At the horizon I use 15x NTM EPS (~31% below the 21.7x median, at the enterprise-software sub-median of ~15.6x, inside the range) and 11.5x forward EV/EBITDA (~30% below the ~16.3x estimated forward median, inside the range).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The ~30% discount rests on company facts that persist through Oct-2027, not on sell-side calls. (1) Management calls FY27-FY28 the peak capex years ($90-95B gross, <=$70B net) and will not give an FCF-positive date, so FCF stays negative through at least May 2028 (TTM ~-$28.7B). (2) Credit: S&P BBB- (stable outlook since the 2026-07-09 cut) and Moody's Baa2 negative, with record CDS of ~200-222bp, against A-or-better hyperscaler peers. Further financing of ~$20-40B is likely in Jan-May 2027. (3) Concentration: per S&P, ~half of the $664B RPO is OpenAI, which is loss-making and whose IPO-announcement odds before Jun-2027 are only ~50% on Kalshi. (4) The non-GAAP to GAAP EPS gap is ~23% (Q1 $1.92 vs $1.56), versus near-GAAP reporting at the hyperscalers. Offsetting this, ORCL has the fastest EPS growth in the set (+35% FY28), so I stay at the enterprise-software sub-median rather than at the bottom (ADBE 8.5x). Re-rating to the 21.7x median would need FCF visibility. That is my bull case, not my base.

thesis_break_reason: $95 is ~17% below the $114.50 52-week low. There the market cap (~$290B) is only ~3x net debt ex leases (~$97B today, ~$140B at horizon), and EV is ~11x TTM and ~8.5x NTM EBITDA for a business growing revenue ~30%. That would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than volatility: OpenAI re-scoping or deferring its ~$300B commitment, a cut to high yield (needs an S&P notch from a stable outlook, so not base-rate likely), forcing deeply dilutive equity, or multi-site power delays pushing FY28 revenue well below ~$115B.

reasoning: Round 2 keeps the round-1 structure and fixes the facts the supervisor flagged, each verified. FY28 consensus is $11.00 non-GAAP: the $9.13/9.14 figure is the Zacks GAAP-like basis (its Q2 FY27 $1.57 vs the $1.85-1.93 guide confirms it). SAP is 21.5x on USD EPS $9.60, so the 10-peer CY2027 median is 21.7x. Net debt excludes operating leases: notes $125.3B + ~$9B finance leases - $37.1B cash = ~$97B today; my roll-forward with S&P's ~-$42B FY27 FOCF, dividends and ~$8B of 2027 equity gives ~$140B at Oct-2027. TTM FCF is ~-$28.7B. S&P is BBB- stable and Moody's Baa2 negative. Kalshi's OpenAI-IPO-by-Jun-2027 is ~50%, not 75%. NTM at Oct-2027 is 8/12 FY28 + 4/12 FY29. I also raised FY29 from $12.3 to $13.4, because $12.3 was ~20% below the consensus-implied ~$15.4 (Zacks FY29/FY28 = 1.40) without my saying so. I now state a ~13% FY29 haircut and ~9% on NTM. Alternative-lane updates: two GPU trackers (OCPI-B200 $7.71, edging down; 20-provider median $6.64, flat over 90 days, +17% y/y) replace the single-newsletter +79% claim, so AI compute demand looks firm, not surging. Aterio's Wisconsin delay and the Jupiter force majeure still justify the FY28 haircut. Social and newsletter takes (Zitron, Reddit, Substack) are colour only. Valuation: P/E 15x x $11.33 = $170 (60%) and EV/EBITDA 11.5x x ~$57B less $140B over 3.13B shares = $166 (40%), blended to $168. Both multiples are inside the peer ranges, ~30% below the medians, at the enterprise-software sub-median. The discount is justified by persistent negative FCF through the peak-capex years, a BBB-/Baa2-negative rating vs A-rated hyperscalers, and OpenAI concentration. Scenarios: bear $88 (26%), base $168 (51%), bull $245 (23%), as lognormals with sigma 0.32/0.25/0.24. The mixture mean is ~$165 (~$3 below fair value because of the fatter bear tail), the median ~$159, and implied log-dispersion ~47%, near the 56% realized and above the ±25-35% large-cap base rate, as befits a binary-ish financing/counterparty story. P(>=143) = 0.59, up from 0.55: corrected net debt, NTM weights and FY29 outweigh lower IPO odds and the discounted GPU surge. My fair value ($168) is above the supervisor's ~$159 mainly because I keep 15x on a consensus-closer NTM ($11.33) and use a forward peer EV/EBITDA basis. Research this round was 8 searches/fetches; forward peer EBITDA remained inaccessible, so forward EV/EBITDA multiples are TTM rolled by growth (labelled estimates).
